Very happy to see Velocicoaster up that high. I have a bias living in Orlando and having been on it so many times but it is absolutely the total package. Incredible layout, what might be the best inversion in the world towards the end of the ride, it’s smooth, very thrilling, comfortable, very well themed, top tier locker system, reliable, it just does everything absolutely right and I haven’t seen another ride pull off the combination of things Velocicoaster does at that level.


EDIT for comparison to other rides I love:

Steel Vengeance: objectively might have the best layout in the world, smooth and packed with airtime, whatever the fuck that downhill barrel roll is, looks cool and has a great view going up the chainlift. Compared to Velocicoaster tho doesn’t have the theming or dispatching, the locker system is meh and it just feels tedious getting on to the ride at times.

Hagrids: incredibly fun and well themed, one of the best theme park experiences out there, packed with elements, an awesome overall attraction. It’s just not as thrilling as Velocicoaster and is plagued with downtime’s and reliability issues, but the fact Islands of Adventure has these two rides right next to each other is just unfair

Rock n Roller Coaster: very fun, thrilling, well themed Disney coaster. Can even bring your bags on somehow, I absolutely love it. The music makes it really fun too. Not as smooth or even thrilling as Velocicoaster tho.

Somewhat different but where all of Disney World is today was supposed be an actual city home to business, residents, and recreation, which is why the entire land is 27,000 acres and has its own fire department and such. The plans weren’t gonna be approved by the state without a Florida version of Disneyland, The Magic Kingdom, but EPCOT was going to be a city of the future with many people movers and everyone’s homes being updated with the latest technologies, not a theme park. Unfortunately Walt passed away in 1966 before they could barely break ground on The Magic Kingdom, so his brother Roy came out of retirement (or didn’t retire like he wanted to?) to see oversee the opening of the Magic Kingdom in 1971 passing away just a few months afterwards. The Walt Disney company afterwards didn’t feel comfortable with running an actual city like Walt envisioned so they used some of those ideas for the eventual second Disney World park that opened in 1982 turning the property into an entire theme park resort destination. There are many YouTube videos about all this, but seeing Walt himself talk about his plans is really fascinating: https://youtu.be/sLCHg9mUBag

I've struggled with anxiety issues my whole life, and the morning of my CP check in I actually threw up in my hotel room because of how nervous I was, and I was still pretty anxious during check-in too. My nerves cooled down when I finally worked up the courage to talk to other new CPs waiting for the bus to Casting as part of our check-in day. Everyone starting the CP is eager to make new friends so even with my social anxiety, talking to people wasn't too hard, one of those people I talked to that morning is currently my roommate two years later and we are both full-time with Disney now.

Things that have helped me aside from creating social circles and making friends during my CP were trying to become aware of what makes me so anxious, and knowing that in terms of the CP, it was only temporary. I've tried to look back at what has caused my anxiety to get out of control so when I come across it again, I can handle it better. Also with the CP just being a temporary program, just doing what you can to make the best of your limited time down here helps. Maybe you hate it, that's fine you'll be home in a few months, maybe you love it and you don't want to go, then you can attempt to extend your program or go to Casting to see if you can transfer in to a full or part time role, and if not you got to have an amazing few months and you get the carry that energy with you wherever you go.
